## Customer portal — sold or promised, but not delivered

### P1-22. One-click apps: 4 of the 5 are never installed, and the "admin password" was never created

**Files:** `worker/apps.ts:81-110, :152-166, :174-177`; `components/customer/cpanel/AppsPanel.tsx:41-49, :70-73`;
`components/customer/cpanel/shared.tsx:65-67`; `lib/actions-apps.ts:201`

Only `wordpress` has an installer. **ghost, nextcloud, joomla and matomo** (`lib/cpanel-types.ts:42-77`)
get `cat > index.html` containing *"<App> is ready to install"* — then `:174-177`
unconditionally writes `status: "ACTIVE"`. The panel promises *"the application in one step."*

Worse, `AppsPanel.tsx:41-49` shows **Admin user / Admin password** in a `SecretCard` labelled *"Save
these now — shown only once and cannot be retrieved later"*. `adminPassEnc` appears in exactly three
places repo-wide: written (`lib/actions-apps.ts:201`), nulled on success (`worker/apps.ts:176`),
nulled on failure (`:192`). **It is never decrypted.** And `installWordpress` only downloads core and
writes `wp-config.php` — `wp core install` appears nowhere in the repo, so no WordPress account is
created at all.

*Failure:* customer installs Ghost, sees a green `ACTIVE` pill and a live link, clicks it, and gets a
static "Ghost is ready to install" page. Or installs WordPress, saves the credentials exactly as
instructed, and is met by WP's own setup wizard demanding a brand-new admin user — the saved password
opens nothing.

### P1-23. Game settings never reach the VM, and "Server type" is a total no-op

**Files:** `worker/game-config.ts:39, :71-96, :287`; `components/customer/GameSettings.tsx:84-100`;
`lib/actions-game-config.ts:110`

`worker/game-config.ts:39` gates the real apply on `ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG === "1"`. Production `.env`
contains `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION` and `ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` — **this flag is absent**. The simulation
branch writes a marker and notifies *"Game settings applied on <hostname>"* with **no** sandbox
qualifier (the `(sandbox)` suffix at `:93` requires `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, which production does not set).
`server.properties` is never touched.

Separately the "Server type" select (Vanilla / Paper / Purpur / Fabric / Forge) persists
`Server.gameVariant`, which the worker reads **only to build the notification string** (`:68, :93`).
`applyRealConfig(server, family, values)` does not take the variant — so even with the flag on, no jar
is ever swapped.

Also write-only: `_appliedVariant` / `_appliedAt` / `_configVersion` (`:78-83`) are read by nothing and
are silently deleted by the next save (`lib/actions-game-config.ts:110` overwrites `gameConfig` with
validated values only).

### P1-24. The webmail "Identity" panel never reaches the wire

**Files:** `lib/actions-mail.ts:430-441`; `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:166-178`;
`components/customer/mail/MailSettings.tsx:222, :260`

Outgoing mail is compiled as `sendMail({ from: cred.address, to, cc, bcc, subject, text, html,
attachments, inReplyTo, references })` — no `replyTo`, no `headers`, no display name. `cred` is
`{address, password}` only. Grep for `replyTo|organization|displayName` across `lib/actions-mail.ts`
and `lib/mail/**` returns nothing. All three fields are written and read back **only to refill the
form**, and `lib/mailcow.ts` has no mailbox-rename helper.

*Failure:* a business sets **Reply-To** to `support@acme.com` — the field is even email-validated,
which makes it look load-bearing — so replies reach the shared helpdesk. Every reply goes to the
individual instead, silently, until someone notices the helpdesk is empty. The section header claims
*"Identity — How you appear to people you email from this mailbox"* and the hint states *"Replies are
directed here instead of your sending address."*

The signature pipeline immediately beside it **is** fully wired end-to-end
(`MailClient.tsx:125-155` → `Composer.tsx:167-186`), so this is a genuine gap, not house style. Auto-reply
and forwarding are also store-only but carry honest amber banners — those are not counted here.

### P1-25. Bandwidth is never metered — the billing panel is hardwired to zero and abuse detection cannot fire

**Files:** `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx:56, :228-281`; `worker/abuse.ts:8, :25, :32, :35`

`Server.bwInBytes` / `bwOutBytes` have five references repo-wide: the billing read, and three reads in
`worker/abuse.ts`. **Nothing increments either column.** Confirmed against the live DB: every server
row is `bwInBytes = 0, bwOutBytes = 0`.

*Failure:* the panel titled *"Transfer used this cycle across your servers versus plan allowance"*
permanently reads `0 B / 20 TB · 0%`, and both warning branches (`:267` over-allowance, `:272`
approaching-limit) are unreachable. Knock-on: `worker/abuse.ts:8` documents the counter as *"updated
by the metering sweep"* — no such sweep exists, so `deltaBytes` is always 0 and `BANDWIDTH_SPIKE` can
never fire. The platform ships an abuse-detection subsystem that cannot detect anything.

### P1-26. Two more deploy-wizard promises with no implementation

* **"Malware scanner"** (`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:370`) — *"Blocks malicious files and
  suspicious activity (ClamAV)"*. `worker/index.ts:120` installs the packages and enables only
  `clamav-freshclam`, the signature **updater**. Repo-wide there is no `clamscan`, no `clamonacc`, no
  on-access config, no scheduled scan. No file is ever scanned.
* **"Free IPv6 is always included"** (`DeployWizard.tsx:402`, printed on the paid dedicated-IP card).
  `Server.ipv6` is only ever written to `null` (`worker/index.ts:529`); no allocator exists. Confirmed
  in production: every server has `ipv6 = null`.

## Customer portal — status that cannot reflect reality

### P1-27. SSL: the auto-renew switch is inert and an expired certificate renders as healthy

**Files:** `components/customer/SslManager.tsx:124-140`; `lib/actions-ssl.ts:130`;
`worker/ssl.ts:306-329`; `prisma/schema.prisma:901`

`SslCertificate.autoRenew` is written by the switch and read **only** for display
(`app/dashboard/ssl/page.tsx:30`, `SslManager.tsx:127,132,137`). `worker/ssl.ts` exports only
`sslIssue` (one-shot `SSL_ISSUE`); no sweep in `worker/index.ts:1027-1095` touches `sslCertificate`.
`status` / `expiresAt` are written once at issuance and never refreshed — `EXPIRED`, documented in the
schema, is **never written anywhere**.

*Failure:* certificate issued 1 Jan, expires 1 Apr. On 2 Apr the dashboard still shows a green pulsing
`ACTIVE` dot, a green auto-renew switch and a neutral "Expires" date, while every visitor's browser
shows `NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID`. Toggling the switch changes nothing in either direction.

*Minor, same file:* `ISSUING` is missing from `statusColors` (`components/ui/primitives.tsx:71-99`), so
a certificate mid-issuance renders as the grey `STOPPED` dot.

### P1-28. A lapsed domain reads "active" forever and stays fully operable

**Files:** `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:125`; `worker/billing.ts:464-471`

`DomainStatus.EXPIRED` is read in three UI places, but `grep 'status: "EXPIRED"'` across the repo
returns **nothing** — every writer only ever produces ACTIVE / FAILED / PENDING / TRANSFER_*.
`domainAutoRenewSweep` filters on `autoRenew: true`, so a customer who turned auto-renew off is never
revisited by anything.

*Failure:* the domain page shows a green pulsing `active` dot beside a red `expired 151 days ago`
badge; `active === true` keeps the entire DNS manager and the **Renew now** button enabled; and
renewal is quoted at the normal rate for a name that is now in registry redemption (where the real
cost is 5–10×).

### P1-29. Business email: a hardcoded badge, and a verification step that gates nothing

**Files:** `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:345, :96-97, :236`; `app/dashboard/email/page.tsx:51-55`;
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:112, :117, :418-480, :491-539, :624`;
`components/customer/EmailDnsSetup.tsx:91, :106, :137-139`

`EmailHosting.tsx:345` is the literal `<Badge tone="amber">Provisioning</Badge>`. `MailboxRow` has no
`status` field and the page deliberately drops `m.status` — while the real column moves to `ACTIVE`,
`FAILED` and `SUSPENDED`.

*Failure:* Mailcow is down when the mailbox is added; `provisionMailboxOnMailcow` catches and sets
`FAILED`, `addMailbox` still returns `{ok:true}`, and the row reads "Provisioning" **forever** while
mail to it bounces. The two actions that would fix it — `retryMailboxProvision` (`:545`) and
`setMailboxSuspended` (`:606`) — have zero callers, and there is no retry control in the UI.

Separately, `verifyEmailDomain` only writes `verified: true`, and `.verified` is consumed **only for
rendering**. `addMailbox` has no verification check and provisions immediately. Three statements in the
product are therefore false: *"mail starts flowing once verification succeeds"*, *"Mail won't flow
until… verification succeeds"*, and *"DNS verified — mail is now enabled for this domain"*. A customer
who adds only the TXT record gets a green "mail is enabled" badge with no MX record and receives
nothing. **This is the same missing `verified` gate that P0-1 turns into a cross-tenant takeover.**

### P1-30. A registration stuck in "needs review" spins forever with the reason hidden

**Files:** `lib/actions-domains.ts:251`; `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:134, :141-153`;
`components/AutoRefresh.tsx:8`

`lib/actions-domains.ts:251` correctly keeps the charge and leaves `status: "PENDING"` with
`error: "NEEDS REVIEW — registrar status unconfirmed: …"` — the right call, since refunding blind
could give away a domain we paid for. But no sweep ever revisits it (`worker/billing.ts:255` handles
only `TRANSFER_PENDING`) and no admin action resolves it.

*Failure:* the page mounts `<AutoRefresh />` on a 5 s timer for any PENDING domain and states *"This
page refreshes automatically — it usually completes within a minute."* It never will. `domain.error`
is rendered **only** in the `FAILED` branch, so the customer never sees why, and there is no admin
queue for these.

### P1-31. Affiliate commission tiers are decoration

**Files:** `app/dashboard/affiliate/page.tsx:132-170`; `lib/affiliate.ts:45-49`;
`lib/actions-growth.ts:263`

The page shows Starter $5 / Pro $8 / Elite $12 per referral, a live tier badge, and *"N more paying
referrals to reach the Elite tier ($12.00 / referral)"*. `AFFILIATE_TIERS` is imported by that page and
nothing else. The credit actually paid is the flat `referralRewardCents()` (default 500 — and see
P1-8, which is the same number the admin panel cannot change).

*Failure:* a customer reaches 15 paying referrals, watches the badge flip to `Elite — $12.00 /
referral`, and is credited $5.00 — the same as referral #1, forever.

### P1-32. Every notification preference is write-only

**Files:** `components/customer/NotificationPrefs.tsx`; `lib/actions-prefs.ts:19`;
`app/dashboard/settings/page.tsx:48`; `lib/mailer.ts`

Complete reader set for the preference columns: the settings page (to set `defaultChecked`) and the
GDPR export route. `lib/mailer.ts` never loads the user or consults preferences, and none of its
callers do (`lib/actions.ts:136`, `lib/stripe.ts:255`, `lib/actions-account.ts:130, 172`). All ~35
`db.notification.create` sites write unconditionally.

Two toggles are worse than inert: **"Product updates"** governs campaigns sent to
`db.newsletterSubscriber` *by email address* (`lib/actions-newsletter-campaign.ts:193`), a table with
no link to `User`; **"Security alerts — new sign-ins and changes to tokens or 2FA"** governs a channel
that was never built (login / token / 2FA paths write audit rows only).

*Failure:* customer turns all three off, sees "Saved ✓", and the next wallet top-up still emails a
receipt. For a UK/EU customer this is a marketing-consent problem, not just a UX one.

## Customer portal — controls that report success without effect

### P1-33. Three domain "saved — applied once the domain is active" promises with no applier

**Files:** `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:112`; `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:324-330, :492-496`;
`lib/actions-domains.ts:195-202`; `lib/domain-transfer.ts:154-168`;
`components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx:214-217`

Nameservers → `Domain.nameservers`, read only for form prefill and GDPR export. URL redirects →
`Setting["domain-redirect:{id}"]`; registrar lock → `Setting["domain-lock:{id}"]` — both keys are
referenced **only inside `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`**. Neither the PENDING→ACTIVE transition nor
`settleCompletedTransferIn` replays any of them.

*Failure:* customer sets custom nameservers and enables the registrar lock while the domain is
PENDING, gets the green *"…applied at the registrar once it activates"*, the domain goes ACTIVE a
minute later, and nothing is pushed. The lock card then prints *"Currently locked (saved — applies
once the registrar is connected)"* permanently.

### P1-34. Clearing all nameservers returns a green "Saved." while the registrar keeps the old delegation

**Files:** `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:96, :112`; `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:65-69`

The registrar call sits inside `if (unique.length >= 2)`. With both fields cleared `unique.length ===
0`: the block is skipped entirely — no `setNameservers`, no `note` — `:112` writes `[]`, and the client
falls through to `res.note ?? "Saved."` in emerald.

*Failure:* a customer reverting from Cloudflare back to name.com's DNS clears both fields, sees
"Saved.", and the delegation is unchanged — permanently. **There is no path in the product to undo a
nameserver delegation.**

### P1-35. The WHOIS-privacy switch never contacts the registrar

**Files:** `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152`; `components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:157, :176-195`;
`app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115`; `lib/registrar.ts:137`

The action does one `db.domain.update` and returns — no `nc(...)` call, unlike its siblings at `:99`
and `:186`. It is presented as a live pill switch with an optimistic flip, above copy describing a
real-world effect, and the Setup checklist un-ticks *"WHOIS privacy on"*. Registration always sets
`privacyEnabled: true` at the registrar.

*Failure:* a business that needs public WHOIS (some TLD registries and B2B verification flows require
it) flips it off, the switch greys out, the checklist un-ticks, and their details stay redacted at
name.com. The returned `note` is honest; the switch and the checklist are not.

### P1-36. The DNS panel hardcodes "name.com DNS" regardless of actual delegation

**Files:** `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:243, :78, :327`;
`components/customer/DomainAdvanced.tsx:87`

`:243` is a fixed `<Badge tone="brand">name.com DNS</Badge>` and `:78` loads records from name.com's
zone API. `Domain.nameservers` is in scope at `:327` and never consulted — even though the Advanced
card explicitly warns *"Setting custom nameservers moves DNS off name.com's servers."*

*Failure:* after moving DNS to Cloudflare, the table still lists the dead name.com zone, and Quick
setup / Add record / Import all write into it and report success. The customer adds an MX record, sees
"Added 1", and mail never routes.

### P1-37. The header Start/Stop/Reinstall/Delete buttons swallow every refusal

**File:** `components/ServerControls.tsx:18-21`

```ts
startTransition(() => serverAction(serverId, action));
```

The result is never read, there is no `.catch`, and the component has no error state at all.
`serverAction` refuses three ways: a silent `return` when a job is in flight (`lib/actions.ts:476`),
and a `throw` for suspended servers (`:456-458`) and for attached volumes (`:464-471`).

*Failure:* a server with an attached volume — the customer clicks **Reinstall**, accepts the "wipes ALL
data" confirm, and nothing happens. The carefully written explanation ("Detach your data volume(s)
first…") goes into an unhandled rejection that Next redacts in production. The sibling `ReinstallOs`
in the Resize tab handles the identical refusal correctly (`ReinstallOs.tsx:230-231`), so the same
error is explained in one place on the page and invisible in the other.

### P1-38. Control-panel service buttons and "Enable SSL" report stale state

**Files:** `components/customer/cpanel/CronServicesPanel.tsx:163-168`;
`components/customer/cpanel/WebsitesPanel.tsx:44`; `lib/actions-websites.ts:262-268`

The services panel refreshes 2500 ms after enqueue, but the worker polls every 3000 ms
(`worker/index.ts:34`) and runs jobs strictly serially platform-wide. There is no second refresh and no
per-row pending state.

*Failure:* customer clicks **Stop** on nginx; the row keeps reading green `● running` indefinitely, so
they click Stop three more times — queuing three more jobs — before finding the manual Refresh.

`WebsitesPanel.tsx:44` gates its 4 s poll on `["PENDING","DELETING"]`, but `requestWebsiteSsl` — unlike
`createWebsite`/`toggleWebsite` — never sets `PENDING`. Clicking "Enable SSL" leaves the SSL column at
`—` and surfaces neither success nor `Website.error` until a full page reload.

### P1-39. "Live resource snapshot" CPU is the since-boot average

**Files:** `lib/cpanel-inline.ts:126, :163`; `components/customer/cpanel/CronServicesPanel.tsx:63, :72-73`

`:126` takes a **single** sample of `/proc/stat`'s cumulative jiffies and `:163` divides busy by total —
the mean since boot. No previous sample, no delta. The UI labels it *"Live resource snapshot"* with an
*"auto-refreshing"* badge polling every 8 s.

*Failure:* on a 30-day-old idle VM the customer pegs all cores at 100%; this bar sits at ~2% and creeps
by hundredths per refresh, while the Overview tab's Proxmox-fed "Live stats" card **on the same page**
(`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:227-232`) correctly shows 100%. Two contradictory CPU numbers,
one screen.

### P1-40. A Claude build that reaches `AWAITING_APPROVAL` becomes unapprovable and then locks the account

**Files:** `components/customer/ClaudeBuilder.tsx:37, :90`; `app/dashboard/build/page.tsx:68, :71-103`;
`lib/actions-claude.ts:22, :28, :69-87, :118, :150`; `worker/claude.ts:239, :249`

The Approve/Reject buttons live only in `ClaudeBuilder`, gated on a `buildId` held purely in React
state. The page mounts `<ClaudeBuilder servers={servers} />` with no build prop, and the "Recent
builds" table renders no row id, link or control. `approveBuild`/`rejectBuild` are the only exits; the
worker returns early unless `QUEUED`/`PLANNING`, and there is no reaper.

*Failure:* planning takes up to 90 s, so the user reloads. The build lands in `AWAITING_APPROVAL`,
which is in `ACTIVE_STATUSES` — so `submitBuild` now refuses every retry on that host (*"A build is
already in progress on this server"*), and after three orphans `MAX_ACTIVE_BUILDS_PER_USER` refuses
**all** builds on **all** servers, permanently, with no customer-reachable escape.
`AWAITING_APPROVAL` also has no `statusColors` entry, so the one status demanding action renders as
the neutral grey `STOPPED` dot.

### P1-41. API tokens: the `write` scope grants nothing, and "N active" counts expired tokens

**Files:** `app/api/v1/servers/route.ts:20`; `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx:205-213, :250-256, :301-303`;
`lib/api-auth.ts:53-55, :79-88`

`find app/api/v1 -name route.ts` returns exactly one file, `GET` only, requiring `servers:read`. The UI
mints `read`/`write`. Tracing `["write"]` through `tokenHasScope`: not `*`, not `servers:read`, no
`servers:*`, and the `action === "read"` rescue needs the literal `read` — **false on every branch**.

*Failure:* a user builds a deploy integration, unchecks read and checks write, and gets a token the
settings list badges as active with scope `write` that 403s on the only endpoint that exists.

Separately, `:301-303` counts `!t.revoked` as "active" while the row badge at `:250-256` flags the same
token `expired` and `lib/api-auth.ts:53-55` 401s it — the header reads "1 active" above a row reading
"expired".

### P1-42. Webmail attachments can be fetched from the wrong mailbox

**Files:** `components/customer/mail/ReadingPane.tsx:174`; `app/api/mail/attachment/route.ts:19`;
`lib/mail/imap.ts:95-101`

`ReadingPane.tsx:174` builds `/api/mail/attachment?folder=…&uid=…&part=…` with **no `mailbox=`** —
`ReadingPane` is never given the active address (every other call site threads `activeAddress`
through). The route reads `sp.get("mailbox")` and `resolveMailbox(undefined)` falls back to
`boxes[0]`, the oldest mailbox.

*Failure:* a user with `sales@` (created first) and `jane@` switches to `jane@` and clicks a PDF. The
server opens `sales@`'s INBOX at that UID — best case a 404, worst case they download a different
message's attachment from a different mailbox. Same account, so not cross-tenant, but it is silently
wrong data.

*Also in the mail client:* **Starred** maps to the inbox path and filters one 50-message page pinned to
page 1 (`MailClient.tsx:191, 204-209`), so a starred message that gets archived or pushed past 50 shows
"This folder is empty" — the flag is still set server-side, there is just no cross-folder `\Flagged`
search. **Snoozed** is an *enabled* rail item whose path resolves to `null` (`:190`), rendering "New
mail will show up here" for a feature that does not exist — inconsistent with the honest `disabled` +
"coming soon" treatment given to the Snooze and Filters buttons. **Storage** reports `0` on probe
failure: `getMailboxes` initialises `usedBytes = 0` and swallows IMAP errors
(`lib/actions-mail.ts:70-90`), so the *"live usage is unavailable"* fallback
(`MailSettings.tsx:1088`) is unreachable and a 4 GB mailbox with a failing quota probe renders "0 B of
5 GB, 0% used" — the near-full warning can never fire.
